subject: Science
title: Science Exam 7
topic: Motion & Pressure · Periodic Table · Investigative skills
intro: AQA Higher style. You may use a calculator. Write the equation, convert units first (km → m, minutes → s), and always give the unit with your answer. Write full sentences for the longer answers.

questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate pressure?
questions.ms: Pressure = force ÷ area.

questions.q:
A runner runs 2.4 km in 10 minutes.
Calculate the runner's average speed in m/s.
questions.ms: 4 m/s. M1 2.4 km = 2400 m and 10 min = 600 s, M1 speed = distance ÷ time, A1 2400 ÷ 600 = 4.

questions.q:
A train travels at a steady speed of 40 m/s for 2.5 minutes.
Calculate the distance it travels, in kilometres.
questions.ms: 6 km. M1 2.5 min = 150 s, M1 distance = speed × time = 40 × 150 = 6000 m, A1 6 km.

questions.q: Two cyclists ride side by side in the same direction, both at 6 m/s. State their relative speed and describe how each cyclist appears to the other.
questions.ms: Relative speed is 0 m/s (1); each cyclist appears not to be moving / stationary to the other (1).

questions.q: Calculate the car's average speed for the first 45 seconds of the journey. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.ms: 7.8 m/s. M1 total distance ÷ total time = 350 ÷ 45, A1 7.8 (7.77…).

questions.q: Was the car faster in section A or section C? Use the graph to explain how you can tell.
questions.ms: Section A (1): the line is steeper / speed in A = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 m/s compared with 10 m/s in C (1).

questions.q:
A table exerts a pressure of 1500 Pa on the floor. The total area of its four legs touching the floor is 0.02 m².
Calculate the weight of the table.
questions.ms: 30 N. M1 pressure = force ÷ area, so force = pressure × area, M1 1500 × 0.02, A1 30 N.

questions.q:
A student weighs 500 N. Each of her shoes has an area of 125 cm² touching the ground.
Calculate the pressure she exerts on the ground when standing on both feet, in N/cm².
questions.ms: 2 N/cm². M1 total area = 2 × 125 = 250 cm², M1 pressure = force ÷ area = 500 ÷ 250, A1 2 N/cm².

questions.q: Explain why a sharp knife cuts food more easily than a blunt knife. Use the equation for pressure in your answer.
questions.ms: Pressure = force ÷ area (1); a sharp blade has a much smaller area in contact with the food (1); so the same force gives a bigger pressure (1).

questions.q: More air is pumped into a bicycle tyre. Explain, in terms of particles, why the pressure inside the tyre increases.
questions.ms: More air particles in the same volume (1); so particles collide with the inside wall of the tyre more often / more collisions per second (1); each collision exerts a force on the wall (1); so a bigger total force on the same area, so a bigger pressure (1).

questions.q:
A diver swims down from the surface of the sea to a depth of 20 m. A climber climbs from sea level to the top of a high mountain.
Explain how the pressure on the diver and the pressure on the climber change. Use ideas about weight and particles in your answer.
questions.ms: Level 3 (5-6): both changes correctly described and explained with weight and particles. Level 2 (3-4): both changes described with some explanation, or one fully explained. Level 1 (1-2): simple statements of the changes. Diver: pressure increases with depth; more water above, so more weight pushing down; water is incompressible and passes the pressure on in all directions. Climber: atmospheric pressure decreases with height; less air above, so less weight of air pushing down; air is less dense higher up, so fewer particles in each cm³ and fewer collisions with a surface each second.

questions.q:
Mo pushes on a door handle with a force of 15 N. The handle is 0.8 m from the hinge.
Calculate the moment of the force.
questions.ms: 12 Nm. M1 moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot = 15 × 0.8, A1 12 Nm.

questions.q:
A see-saw is balanced. A man weighing 600 N sits 1.2 m to the left of the pivot. His daughter weighs 450 N.
How far to the right of the pivot must she sit, in metres?
questions.ms: 1.6 m. M1 anticlockwise moment = clockwise moment, M1 600 × 1.2 = 450 × d, so 720 = 450 × d, A1 d = 720 ÷ 450 = 1.6 m.

questions.q: Explain why it is easier to open a door by pushing near the handle than by pushing near the hinge.
questions.ms: Moment = force × distance from the pivot (1); the handle is further from the hinge, so the same force gives a bigger turning effect / less force is needed (1).

questions.q:
Potassium reacts quickly with water and burns with a lilac flame. Caesium is further down Group 1.
Predict how caesium reacts with water compared with potassium, and describe the trend in melting point going down Group 1.
questions.ms: Caesium reacts more violently / faster / may explode (1) because reactivity increases going down Group 1 (1). Melting point decreases going down Group 1 (1).

questions.q: Going down Group 7, the halogens…
questions.ms: Become darker in colour. They also become less reactive and their melting points increase.

questions.q: Going down Group 0 (the noble gases), the boiling point…
questions.ms: Increases (helium −269 °C up to radon −62 °C).

questions.q:
A student places a heavy block on damp sand. She changes the area of the block's base touching the sand and measures the depth of the dent it makes.
Name the independent variable and the dependent variable.
questions.ms: Independent: area of the base touching the sand (1). Dependent: depth of the dent (1).

questions.q:
Her results:
Area (cm²)Depth of dent (mm)
1016
208
404
802
Describe the relationship between the area and the depth of the dent.
questions.ms: As the area increases, the depth decreases (negative relationship) (1). When the area doubles, the depth halves (inversely proportional) (1).

questions.q: Another student compares the dents made by four kinds of shoe: trainer, high heel, boot and snowshoe. Which type of graph should he draw?
questions.ms: Bar chart, because the type of shoe is a categoric variable.

questions.q: The student measured the depth of each dent with a ruler, judging it by eye. Suggest one improvement to the method and explain how it would help.
questions.ms: Improvement (1): use a depth gauge or the depth rod of a vernier caliper / smooth the sand flat the same way each time / repeat each test and take a mean. Explanation (1): more precise readings / fairer test / reduces the effect of random errors. (A reason alone, with no change to the method, scores 0.)
